title: Cokret Ephemeral Broadcast Envelope
description: Wire shape for broadcast ephemeral signals — ck.presence, ck.typing, ck.receipt.read, ck.call.signal. These signals have wire_scope=ephemeral_event in event-kind-registry.json: they MUST NOT carry CBA reducer fields, MUST NOT advance Seal coverage, governance state_root or actor_seq, MUST NOT enter reducer state, and MUST NOT be submitted via ck.events.submit. They are carried on dedicated ephemeral channels (sync subscribe live stream, presence/typing fanout, call signaling channel) and are dropped at TTL. Point-to-point to-device signals (ck.key.verification.*) use device-message.schema.json instead — they have a sender+recipient pair and do not match this broadcast shape. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §2.3 (wire-scope reject rule) and zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §5 (ephemeral channel transport).

kind.description: Ephemeral signal kind. MUST be one of the four broadcast ephemeral kinds; ck.key.verification.* point-to-point strands MUST use device-message.schema.json instead.

realm_id.description: Realm whose ephemeral channel carries this signal. Authorization to broadcast a signal on a Realm channel is governed by the same membership / capability rules as the corresponding durable kinds.

actor_id.description: Signaling actor. MUST be a member of the Realm (ck.member.state cell join != ban/leave/remove at receive time) for the broadcast to be admitted by other clients; receivers drop signals from non-members without surfacing them.

device_id.description: Originating device. Optional but RECOMMENDED so receivers can dedupe per-device typing/presence signals.

sent_at.description: Wall-clock send time. Diagnostic only — ephemeral signals do not participate in HLC ordering.

expires_at.description: Server / client MUST drop the signal at or after this time. Per-kind soft caps (recommended): presence ≤ 60s, typing ≤ 15s, receipt.read ≤ 30s, call.signal ≤ 30s. Signals with expires_at > sent_at + 5 minutes MUST be dropped by receivers (`invalid_param`).

payload.description: Kind-specific signal payload. Schema per kind is defined by the producing module (e.g. zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md for ck.call.signal, zh/discovery/read-receipts.md for ck.receipt.read). Payload MUST NOT carry mutable governance state — that belongs in a durable event.

proof.description: Detached-JWS proof over the canonical ephemeral envelope, structurally isomorphic to the durable Event proof ($defs/event_proof in event-envelope.schema.json / models/event-and-patch.md §3). Required for ck.call.signal; RECOMMENDED for ck.receipt.read so receivers can verify origin without trusting relay. presence / typing MAY omit proof for cost reasons; receivers MUST NOT promote unsigned signals to durable state. Signing input is the canonical proof binding object {event_digest, actor_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}; event_digest is canonical_digest of the envelope with `proof` removed (RFC 8785 JCS). verification_method MUST be `{actor_id}#{device_id}` where the fragment is the full `ck:device:<uuidv7>` id, and its controller DID MUST equal envelope actor_id. See crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §5.

call_id.description: Typed call/session identifier (ck:call:<uuidv7>) scoped to the Realm. Unified with ice-config-response and media-operations so cross-channel join cross-checks key on the same form.

seq.description: Monotonic per-(realm_id, call_id, actor_id, device_id) sequence. Receivers MUST reject replay or rollback.

data.description: Signal-type-specific payload body (invite/answer/candidate/mute_state/...). Declared as the closed payload field per webrtc-signaling.md §5/§6; optional because some signals (e.g. ack) carry no body. Inner shape is signal_type-specific and intentionally open.

ephemeral_proof.description: Detached-JWS proof for a broadcast ephemeral envelope. Structurally isomorphic to event-envelope.schema.json #/$defs/event_proof: same kind / alg / verification_method / event_digest / created_at / jws shape, so a single EdDSA detached-JWS verifier serves both durable Event proofs and ephemeral signal proofs. The only difference is which canonical bytes feed event_digest (here: the ephemeral envelope with `proof` removed).

kind.description: detached_jws = device signature over the canonical proof binding object canonical_json({event_digest, actor_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}). event_digest is the canonical ephemeral-envelope hash with `proof` removed (RFC 8785 JCS).

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing device key. For ck.call.signal MUST be `{actor_id}#{device_id}` where the fragment is the full `ck:device:<uuidv7>` id; verifier MUST strip the fragment for controller comparison and MUST compare that controller DID bit-identically to the envelope actor_id, then resolve the verify key from the device directory (keys/query device_signing_key, keys-operations.schema.json). Same form as event_proof.verification_method.

alg.description: Default EdDSA. Same enum as event_proof.alg for a shared verifier.

event_digest.description: canonical_digest(envelope without `proof`) per RFC 8785 JCS, isomorphic to event_proof.event_digest (which excludes proofs + unsigned).
